capillary heterogeneity can account for the observed data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the capillary heterogeneity model is a useful tool in the analysis of uptake and elimination data, and that the model is a necessary component in any interpretation of such data.
the effects of capillary heterogeniety on steady uptake of substances are important and should be considered in studies of uptake by intact organs.
capillary heterogeneity is a necessary feature of the intact organ, and that it can be detected by appropriate analysis of elimination data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assumption of functional homogeneity of capillaries in a perfused organ should be tested in each case before it is accepted.
capillary heterogeneity may be a significant factor in the interpretation of steady uptake data from isolated perfused livers.

the capillary heterogeneity is the most likely cause of the observed non-linearity of the uptake rate versus the substrate concentration curve, and the model incorporating the capillary heterogeneities can explain the non-linearity of uptake rate versus substrate concentration curve in the case of the galactose uptake by the isolated perfused pig liver.
